Subject: Adaptive slotting proposal for Orchid Health renewal — capacity plan and next steps

Hi Priya & Taylor,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. We pulled together a short plan that maps Orchid's observed run-rate and peak patterns (attached) to a dedicated capacity change we believe will reduce unit cost while preserving peak latency SLAs. Key idea: "adaptive slotting" — keep a steady committed pool for baseline throughput and add small, reserved slot groups that automatically activate during predictable daily peaks.

What we're proposing in this note:
- Baseline: convert 18 existing A100-equivalent slots into a 14-slot committed pool with sustained KV-cache reservations.
- Peak slots: add 6 flexible A30-class slots that auto-activate on the customer policy during 08:00–20:00 PT; these remain reserve-only outside peak windows to reduce charges.
- Headroom buffer: maintain a 2-GPU quick-burst buffer for unexpected traffic spikes, with an agreed failover to a compatible host in a neighboring region for extreme surges.

Benefits: cheaper committed footprint, lower per-token cost from caching affinity, and predictable smoothing of tail latency during daily spikes (based on the attached usage traces).

Attached: usage_traces_aug2026.csv (sampled traces), and a 2-page Adaptive Slotting proposal (adaptive-slotting-proposal-q3.pdf).

Questions:
1) Is Orchid able to accept a mixed-class GPU footprint (A100 baseline + A30 peaks) for the renewal?
2) What's the procurement timeline for a Q4 start if we finalize terms this week?

If you like the plan, I'll loop in pricing and Marissa for the renewal paperwork and a quick DocuSign to lock dates.

Thanks,

Hi Priya — looping in a quick technical note.

Short answers to your asks:
- SLA: Peak A30 slots will be fronted by the same traffic router and have identical p90 latency SLOs when active. For the rare case an A30 pool degrades, requests automatically fall back to the committed A100 pool (slower throughput per-GPU but preserves correctness). We'll include an explicit fallback chain in the SOW.
- Region: we can pin both the committed and peak pools to us-west-2. The "neighboring region" fallback referenced by Marcus is only for emergency multi-region failover; it will not be used for normal peak activation.

Sizing recommendation based on your attached traces (I sampled the 08:00–20:00 windows across weekdays):
- Baseline committed: 14 A100-equivalent slots with KV cache affinity (same as Marcus suggested).
- Peak flexible: 6 A30 slots triggered at 25%+ burst above baseline sustained for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Buffer: 2 A100 cold-start slots for <5-minute bursts with graceful degradation policy.

Operational notes:
- We will enable prefix caching and sticky routing for sessions pinned to the baseline pool to preserve latency for active sessions when peaks occur.
- Autoscaling policy will be policy-based (time + utilisation threshold) with manual override for scheduled campaigns.

I'll produce a short SOW snippet and a proforma for Marissa to finalize pricing.

Thanks,
